s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with intermittent throbbing and localization to the right lower quadrant, associated with nausea and increased stool frequency, and a complex medical history
salient_findings: Intermittent throbbing abdominal pain localizing to the right lower quadrant
Moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant and positive Rovsing sign
Lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve on CT
No appendix identified on CT or laparoscopy
Biopsy showing acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis
Small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum on repeat CT
key_facts: 49-year-old Caucasian woman
5-day history of abdominal pain
Pain began periumbilically and localized to the right lower quadrant
Associated with nausea and increased stool frequency
History of laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 2009
History of supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy for uterine fibroids in 2012
Endometriosis noted during 2012 surgery
Moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant on examination
Positive Rovsing sign
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count
CT showed lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve
Appendix not identified on CT or laparoscopy
Biopsy of inflamed areas showed acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis
Patient improved initially but returned with sharp right lower quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting
Repeat white-cell count was 13.2×10^9/L
Repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum

shortlist.label: Intestinal endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of endometriosis and biopsy of inflamed areas showed foci of endometriosis

shortlist.label: Small-bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial CT and clinical presentation suggested acute appendicitis, although appendix was not identified

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Terminal ileitis and small-bowel obstruction are consistent with Crohn's disease

shortlist.label: Ileocecal valve syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve on CT suggests possible ileocecal valve syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's history of endometriosis, biopsy showing foci of endometriosis, and symptoms consistent with intestinal involvement support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: Appendix not identified on CT or laparoscopy

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: No prior history or typical findings of Crohn's disease

rejected.label: Ileocecal valve syndrome
rejected.why: Not a well-established diagnosis and does not explain the patient's full range of symptoms

rejected.label: Small-bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While present, it is likely a complication of the underlying condition, intestinal endometriosis
